newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank governor to quit if reform fails.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank governor to quit if reform fails.

text.p: Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Tuesday he will resign if drastic bank stabilisation policies launched by the BNB fail to work.

In yet another move to stabilise the country's wrecked financial system the BNB on Monday placed nine problem banks under special supervision and raised the interest rate to a record high of 300 percent.

"The aim of these measures is to bring down inflation and curb the depreciation of the lev, which in turn will give us the opportunity to lower the interest rate in the near future," Filipov told a news conference.
"I do not expect people to return all their savings in the banks to profit from high yields, but I hope to reverse the process (of withdrawing deposits) a little," he added.

"If we grossly fail, I already have a rough copy of my resignation, which I shall submit to the speaker of parliament," said Filipov. Under Bulgarian laws the central bank goveror is appointed by parliament.

Bankruptcy procedures will not be sought for all of the nine banks placed under special supervision, but only for those which after a trial period fail to improve their capital adequacy and collection of non-performing loans, said Filipov.
Deposits of individuals and companies in the nine banks amount to 17 billion levs.

Deposits in five other banks placed under special supervision in the past few months were guaranteed from the date of the BNB decision to seek their bankruptcy through the courts. However the courts have so far delayed ruling on these insolvencies.
The government will rely on privatisation proceeds to cover deposit guarantees, after the law re-voted by parliament, said Prime Minister Zhan Videnov on Monday.
"We hope that Bulgaria has met the funding conditions of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as far as bank reform and privatisation targets are concerned," said Filipov.
"It remains to be seen what progress in the restructuring area the government has achieved," said Filipov.

Bulgaria hopes to win a second $115 million tranche of IMF funding during IMF/World Bank annual meeting. The IMF postponed the tranche until the government closed 64 state industrial loss-makers and stabilised its financial system.

The cabinet urged parliament to change the deposit guarantee law passed in June, so that deposits are compensated by state from the date of the court declares the banks insolvent, instead of the date they are placed under supervision. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
